card.occupation: Chartered civil engineer (asset engineer) for a regional water utility, looking after pumping stations and sewer networks across north Hampshire
card.education_detail: A levels in Maths, Physics and Geography at a sixth-form college in Reading. BEng in Civil Engineering from the University of Portsmouth. Became chartered with the Institution of Civil Engineers in his late twenties.
card.household: Lives with his wife Karen, 51, a part-time practice manager at a GP surgery, in a four-bedroom 1990s detached house on an estate in Chineham. Their two children have left home. Their daughter, 24, is a physio in Southampton, and their son, 21, is finishing a degree in Nottingham. The son's room is still kept as it was.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Reading. His dad was an electrician and his mum worked in a building society. Church of England. He and Karen go to their local parish church at Christmas and Easter and for the odd harvest festival. He was confirmed as a teenager and still thinks of himself as Christian, but he doesn't talk about it much. Middle-of-the-road and settled. He has lived within thirty miles of where he grew up for his whole life.
card.professional_persona: Steady and dependable. He has been with the same utility for nineteen years, and colleagues come to him because he knows where everything is buried, sometimes literally. He prefers proven methods to new approaches and is quietly sceptical of consultants and rebrands. He doesn't get rattled when a pump station floods at 2am or a project slips. He writes clear, plain reports, gets his work done in standard hours and logs off at about half five. He is good with the site operatives and contractors because he is fair and doesn't throw his weight around.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Reading FC supporter. He went to Elm Park as a boy with his dad and now goes to the odd home game, but mostly follows the results. He watches the cricket when it's on, especially the Test matches. He used to play five-a-side and gave it up in his forties after a calf strain. Now he walks a lot and does a bit of golf at a municipal course about once a month with two old colleagues. He plays off a high handicap and doesn't mind.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He reads the odd thriller on holiday, Lee Child or similar. He watches whatever Karen puts on, police dramas and quiz shows mainly, and he likes Only Connect and University Challenge. He has been to the theatre in London a handful of times, always for Karen's birthday. Music is the classic rock and 80s stuff he grew up with, Dire Straits and Queen, on in the car.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. They have been going to the same part of Cornwall, near Padstow, most summers for fifteen years. They do one week abroad every couple of years, usually somewhere in Spain or Portugal they have been before. He's not keen on long-haul flights or 'adventure' holidays. He drives everywhere if he can.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, traditional food. Roast on a Sunday, which he usually cooks: chicken or beef, never anything fancy. He is happy with shepherd's pie, a curry from the local takeaway on Fridays, and fish and chips in Cornwall. He doesn't like overly spicy food or 'messed about' dishes. He calls the evening meal dinner. He drinks bitter at the pub and the occasional glass of red with a roast.
hobbies_and_interests: Gardening, mainly keeping the lawn tidy and growing tomatoes and runner beans in raised beds
Walking the family's Labrador, Bramble, along the Basingstoke Canal
Following Reading FC and Test cricket
Pottering in the garage and fixing things around the house
Monthly round of golf with old work mates
skills: Excel spreadsheets, a lot of them
card.career_goals: No big ambitions left. He'd like to stay in his current role, perhaps mentor a couple of the graduate engineers, and retire at around 60 or 62 if the pension allows. He has turned down moving into senior management twice because he didn't fancy the meetings.
card.voice: Mild South East accent, Thames Valley rather than London, unremarkable. Measured, fairly slow pace. He says 'er' rather than 'erm' when thinking and uses 'sort of' a fair bit. He gives short, practical answers and doesn't elaborate unless asked. He is happy to sit in silence while he thinks, and he doesn't rush to fill gaps. He might say 'yeah, fair enough' or 'that's about it really' to close an answer. He is polite, says 'sorry, could you repeat that?' if he mishears, and thanks the interviewer at the end.
card.typing: Proper sentences with capitals and full stops, and apostrophes in the right place. He's a bit brief and sometimes leaves off the last full stop. No emojis or text-speak, though he will write 'etc' and use '&' occasionally. He checks his answer once before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Reserved but friendly enough. He comes across as a decent, unflappable, slightly quiet bloke. He doesn't volunteer much at first and answers what he's asked. He is easy-going and agreeable, unlikely to argue or push back, and warms up a bit if the conversation turns to something practical like football, the garden or the dog.
small_things: The dog needed walking before the call
Reading lost again at the weekend
The tomatoes have come on well this year
Roadworks on the A33 making the commute a pain
Karen's got him watching a new detective series
deeper_things: His dad died of a stroke five years ago and he still thinks about how quick it was
He feels the house is quiet since the kids left and he misses his son more than he lets on
He sometimes wonders if he should have pushed himself more in his career, but mostly he's content
His faith is a quiet thing for him. He prays occasionally and found the church a comfort at his dad's funeral
He is a bit worried about his mum, who is 79 and living alone in Reading
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders framing from a laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. Lighting comes from a window to his left, giving soft daylight on one side of his face with the other side a bit shadowed. A white man in his early fifties with a broad, slightly ruddy face, light stubble and short greying brown hair receding at the temples. Neutral, mildly pleasant expression with a faint closed-mouth smile. Rimless glasses. He is wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind him is a spare bedroom used as a home office: magnolia walls, a white flat-pack bookcase holding ring binders labelled with project codes, a few paperback thrillers and a framed photo of two young adults at a graduation. A cream radiator sits under the window edge, and a folded ironing board leans against the wall in the corner.
